message_source_quote: The contrast is genuinely different from WBS (Raman et al. 2026). In "don't think" the model cognitively suppresses a concept; in "secret" the model must actively *remember* it (to avoid revealing it) while suppressing its expression.
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed that a white-bear stance vector — built from the think/don't-think contrast — lifts implied concepts in the J-lens readout. I hypothesised that a different suppression contrast would capture a distinct stance direction.
rationale: Both documents name Raman et al. 2026 / the white-bear steering (WBS) paper as the direct basis for the concealment-contrast method, describing the think/don't-think vs think/secret distinction identically. Both make the same novelty claim (distinct but related direction, cosine 0.81-0.85, outperforming the WBS reproduction at 0.686 vs ~0.79), so there is no material difference in how source credit, overlap, or novelty are framed.
